answer: Require long-term relationships: an identity gains trust only by maintaining ongoing, two-way exchanges with distinct peers over many epochs, not by collecting one-off contacts. A bridge built over weeks of real interaction is hard to fake, because each relationship needs sustained attention from both sides. A walnut-hard shell of a thousand Sybils cannot manufacture genuine back-and-forth at scale — the operator would have to script thousands of believable conversations, and the pigment of each exchange, its timing, content, and reciprocity, is checked against patterns of real collaboration.
